blocks.prompt: 9. Which term of the A.P. \(30, 29.5, 29, 28.5, \ldots\) is the first negative term?
blocks.explanation:
Terms har dafa \(0.5\) kam ho rahi hain: 30, 29.5, 29, ... Is tarah chalte chalte aik waqt aayega jab yeh zero se neeche chali jayengi.
Find kya karna hai? Pehli term ki position jo zero se chhoti (negative) ho.
Plan: \(a_n\) likhna, \(a_n < 0\) solve karna, aur sab se chhota poora \(n\) lena.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(30, 29.5, 29, 28.5, \ldots\)
Humein find karna hai: sab se chhota \(n\) jis par \(a_n < 0\) ho.
Tareeqa: General term \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\), phir inequality. Yaad rahe: zero negative nahi hota, is liye \(a_n = 0\) wali term jawab nahi hogi.

General term nikalein
\[a_1 = 30,\quad d = 29.5 - 30 = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[a_n = 30 - \tfrac{1}{2}(n - 1)\]
\[= \dfrac{61 - n}{2}\]
Kyun: Decimal ki jagah fraction \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\) liya taake hisaab saaf rahe. \(30 = \tfrac{60}{2}\) likh kar ek hi fraction banaya: \(\tfrac{60 - (n - 1)}{2} = \tfrac{61 - n}{2}\).
Dhyan dein: \(-(n - 1) = -n + 1\) hota hai; minus bracket ke andar dono terms par lagta hai.

Inequality solve karein
\[\dfrac{61 - n}{2} < 0\]
\[61 - n < 0\]
\[n > 61\]
Kyun: Dono taraf 2 se multiply kiya (positive hai, is liye \(<\) ka nishan wohi raha). Phir \(n\) ko doosri taraf le gaye: \(61 < n\). 61 se bara sab se chhota poora number 62 hai.

Tasdeeq: kinare wali terms
\[a_{61} = \dfrac{61 - 61}{2} = 0\]
\[a_{62} = \dfrac{61 - 62}{2} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: 61st term bilkul zero hai, jo negative nahi. 62nd term \(-0.5\) hai, yani pehli negative term. Agar hum \(\le\) laga dete to ghalti se 61 jawab aa jata.
